content.text:
I've reviewed every responsive location. Summary of my trace:

- **Article II grant (p0030, p0043)**: the licence is expressly *non-exclusive*, and Vendor retains the right to license others — direction runs against Vendor, not us.
- **Article XXII Right of First Refusal (p0139–p0141)**: a change-of-control first-look on a sale/merger of Licensee, not a sourcing or exclusive-dealing covenant; and if Licensor declines, "Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party."
- **"Field of Use" (p0007)**: scope limit on how we may use Vendor's technology, not a commitment to buy only from Vendor.
- **Article V/VII fees (p0070, p0078)**: volume-based fees and a 33% share of third-party amounts from *Licensed Technology usage* — no requirements commitment or minimum volume routed to the Platform.
- **p0027, p0041, p0085**: restrictions on redistributing Vendor's own technology — licence-scope, not exclusivity.
- No "sole supplier", "all of its requirements", "shall not procure from any third party", or non-compete language anywhere in the document.

input.quote: grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us, so it meets the preferred position. The licence is expressly non-exclusive and runs in Vendor's favour (Licensor may license the technology to others), which is not a restriction on Customer. There is no requirements commitment, minimum volume routed to the Platform, or prohibition on procuring FX platform services from third parties; the fee provisions (p0070, p0078) only price usage of the Licensed Technology and its third-party revenue. The Article XXII Right of First Refusal (p0139–p0141) is a change-of-control first-look on a sale or merger of Licensee, and once the Exercise Period lapses "Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party" — a right-to-match mechanic, not exclusive dealing. The Field of Use definition and the anti-redistribution covenants (p0007, p0027, p0041, p0085) limit how we may use Vendor's technology rather than where we may source competing services; those are licence-scope and IP issues, not exclusivity. No redline proposed under this rule.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
